title: New Jersey Devils tender offer sheet to Utah Mammoth center Barrett Hayton
content:
The New Jersey Devils made one of July 1’s boldest plays on Wednesday evening when they went the offer-sheet route with Utah Mammoth center Barrett Hayton.

The offer sheet is for one year at $4.775 million. If the Mammoth do not match it, the Devils will get Hayton in exchange for a 2027 second-round pick. If Utah does match, they get to keep Hayton, but they are prohibited from trading him for one year. By that point, Hayton will be an unrestricted free agent.

The Mammoth have seven days to make their decision whether to match or not.

The $4.775 million figure is very close to the maximum a team can offer without including a first-round pick as compensation.

The offer sheet is the first in the NHL in two years since the St. Louis Blues successfully offer-sheeted Edmonton Oilers players Dylan Holloway and Philip Broberg in the summer of 2024. The Oilers received second- and third-round picks as compensation.

Hayton, 26, was picked fifth overall by the Arizona Coyotes in the 2018 draft and moved with the franchise to Utah two years ago. He had a down season with only 10 goals and 25 points in 65 games, with his ice time dropping to just 15 minutes per game.

Hayton’s value entering restricted free agency was projected to be approximately $5.37 million on a three-year deal by AFP Analytics, so the offer sheet is relatively close to what he is likely worth on a one-year deal. While not a big offensive driver, he is a strong two-way player and centers are at a premium now across the NHL, especially with how thin the unrestricted free agent class was this summer.

Utah currently has enough cap space to match the Devils’ offer but doing so will put them within a few million of the salary cap. The Mammoth were aggressive on the first day of free agency in signing Anders Lee to a $5.6 million deal and acquiring center Vincent Trocheck via trade.

Those additions likely mean Hayton is in line for only a third-line depth role next season, and Utah’s remaining needs are now primarily on defense. The fact that matching the offer sheet will walk him to UFA status next season lowers his value even more for Utah.

It remains to be seen if this is merely the first of several offer sheets made this offseason as teams attempt to find talent in creative ways given the significant rise in the NHL’s cap and lack of value available in the UFA class.
